title: Emirate of Nejd
capsule: The Emirate of Nejd, conventionally called the Second Saudi State, was the restored realm of the House of Saud on the Nejd plateau of central Arabia, founded in 1824 when Turki ibn Abdullah expelled the remaining Ottoman-Egyptian garrison from Riyadh, which he made his capital. (The state's roots are sometimes dated to 1818, the fall of the First Saudi State to Ibrahim Pasha, hence the wider 1818 starting point.) It reached its height under Faisal ibn Turki but was steadily weakened by succession disputes within the dynasty, allowing the rival Rashidi emirs of Ha'il to encroach. The emirate collapsed at the Battle of Mulayda in January 1891, after which the Saud family went into exile in Kuwait, ending the Second Saudi State decades before Abd al-Aziz ibn Saud's twentieth-century reconquest.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Boundaries of pre-kingdom Nejd are difficult to demarcate precisely; the territory was defined more by tribal confederacies and oasis towns than mapped frontiers, so polygons represent scholarly estimates.
